## PDF page 203

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=203)

```text
                             CHAPTER SIXTEEN



                           SQUEEZING


A squeeze is a specific kind of preflop 3bet where you re-raise after an original
raise gets one or more callers. This is a great way to apply pressure not only
to the original raiser, but also the caller(s) who tend to have capped preflop
calling ranges.

These exercises will guide you through the technical side of squeezing,
including how often different ranges fold against different squeeze sizes and
how often you can expect multiple players to collectively fold preflop.

While this work is mathematically demanding, it will help you build intuition
for the crucial aspects of increasing aggression. When you feel confident
estimating the ranges players originally had, the ranges they would con-
tinue with facing aggression, and the underlying math – it makes pulling the
trigger with weak hands far easier.

Like in previous chapters, we will be working to understand how often we can
expect to pick up the pot uncontested preflop. I.e., how often everyone folds.
Remember that you can find how often everyone will fold by multiplying
every player’s folding frequency together. If the original raiser continues with
20% of their raising range and the caller continues with 50% of their original
calling range, that means both players will fold 40% of the time (80%*50%)
when you raise.


                                   PA G E 2 0 3
```

## PDF page 204

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=204)

```text
                     P O K E R M AT H & P R E F L O P WO R K B O O K


Keep in mind that the continuance ranges are slightly simplified, since the
original caller may very well continue differently if the original raiser calls
or folds. On the other hand, the original raiser may 4bet differently with the
original caller still to act. Static defense ranges are given here to make your
exploration easier, but real-world ranges can be more fluid.

Once again, pay attention and compare the outright success rate of both
squeeze sizes. Using a larger raise size does require more folds to find an
auto-profit squeeze, but finding auto-profit spots will help you feel confident
squeezing bluffs more often.

TOOLS TO USE: Most players should do these exercises with pen & paper. If
you would like to use a tool, download and use the “Multiple Folders” spread-
sheet available at www.splitsuit.pro/sheets

PROCESS: Each page contains a single squeeze scenario. Read the prompt
and begin by filling in the table below. On the left, you have the original range
(o-range) that player entered the pot with and the estimated continuance
range (c-range) against two different squeeze sizes. All ranges are in %-form.




                                      PA G E 2 0 4
```

## PDF page 205

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=205)

```text
                                   S QU E E Z I N G


Remember that your opponent’s folding frequency = 100%-(C-Range/O-
Range). So if they originally entered the pot with 20% of hands and would
continue with 5% of hands after you squeeze, 100%-(5%/20%) = 75%. Which
means you can expect them to fold 75% of the time when you squeeze.

If there are players that have not acted yet (e.g., you squeeze from the SB and
the BB has no o-range), an estimated c-range has been given for the hands
they would continue with facing a squeeze.

After completing the table, answer the questions below and compare your
answers across both squeeze sizes. Keep in mind that the squeeze sizes given
are the total size. E.g., if you are in the SB and there is a 3bb open-raise + 3bb
call and you squeeze to 13bb total, your risk is 12.5bb for a pot of 7.5bb since
your .5bb SB is included in the pot and not your actual risk.

TAKEAWAYS: Pay close attention to the difference between how often both
the original raiser + caller(s) fold compared to how often everyone folds when
there are players left to act. Also, notice the pattern in the BE% related to how
large the squeeze size is and memorize it.

A lot of simplification has been done to keep you focused on your opponent’s
ranges in %-form instead of the exact composition of those ranges. For extra
credit, use your poker software to build o-ranges and subsequent c-ranges
to practice equating %-form and actual composition. Just remember that if
the original callers would 3bet themselves with monster hands, their calling
ranges would not include hands like AA, KK, etc.

GLGL.




                                    PA G E 2 0 5
```
